overlapping_phenotypes: Slowly progressive bilateral peroneal weakness, foot drop, distal muscle wasting, pes cavus, and depressed or absent ankle jerks
discriminating_logic: In dHMN11, sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitudes and conduction velocities remain completely normal while motor studies show reduced CMAPs; CMT2 routinely presents with reduced/unrecordable SNAPs and distal sensory deficits.

overlapping_phenotypes: Distal motor weakness without sensory involvement
discriminating_logic: Classical dHMN11 presents predominantly with early lower limb involvement and delayed motor milestones, whereas dHMN type V initiates primarily in the hand muscles.

overlapping_phenotypes: Distal lower-limb weakness, foot drop, and selective fatty infiltration on muscle MRI
discriminating_phenotype: Coexisting neurogenic EMG abnormalities and dissociated reflex arc
discriminating_logic: Neurogenic EMG abnormalities coexist with myopathic changes in dHMN11 and shows a dissociated reflex arc (ankle jerks lost, patellar jerks preserved/brisk), whereas myopathies lack chronic neurogenic denervation and spare/symmetrically dampen reflexes.

overlapping_phenotypes: Mutations occurring in the same gene (SPTAN1)
discriminating_phenotype: Normal intellectual development and absence of infantile epilepsy
discriminating_logic: dHMN11 patients exhibit completely normal intellectual development, intact language, normal cerebral architecture on brain MRI, and absolute absence of infantile epilepsy.
